summary: The sample is runnable, implements the NBA agents and orchestrator, seeds idempotent demo data, reuses a singleton MongoClient, and writes NBA recommendations to sample_customer_360_03.nba_recommendations. Vector/index work was partially attempted but the MCP index-creation tool failed, so the vector index was not created programmatically. Several gallery expectations (exact dependency pinning, programmatic vector index creation and README guidance for index tuning/cleanup, application-level retries and batched seed writes, and an explicit LangChain agent implementation) are incomplete or deliberately implemented as minimal/deterministic fallbacks to keep the sample runnable without LLM or cloud credentials. See Requirement Results, Practice Checks and Documentation Gaps for line-by-line evidence and the minimal fixes to make the sample gallery-ready.

requirement_results.requirement: The system is written in Python and its agents and orchestrator are built with LangChain (LangChain Python), with the propensity agent, channel agent and timing agent each a separate agent that the orchestrator invokes.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agents.py defines propensity_agent, channel_agent and timing_agent as separate functions (lines 13-31, 34-45, 48-70). The code does not instantiate LangChain Agent objects or use langchain agent APIs.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Wrap the existing functions in lightweight LangChain agent wrappers (or implement LangChain Tools/Agents that call these functions) and update orchestrator to instantiate/use LangChain Agent instances when OPENAI_API_KEY is present.

requirement_results.requirement: A propensity agent reads the customer's interaction history from Azure DocumentDB through a MongoDB-compatible Python driver (e.g. PyMongo) and scores the customer's likelihood of responding to each action type, returning a score per action type.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agents.py propensity_agent reads db.interactions, counts documents and computes scores (lines 17-31).

requirement_results.requirement: A channel agent reads the customer's preference documents from Azure DocumentDB and selects the optimal contact channel for that customer.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agents.py channel_agent finds preferences via db.preferences.find_one and returns the top-ranked channel (lines 38-45).

requirement_results.requirement: A timing agent determines the best send time for contacting the customer.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agents.py timing_agent uses preferences.contact_times or infers next hour (lines 52-70).

requirement_results.requirement: An orchestrator runs the propensity, channel and timing agents for a given customer and combines their outputs into a single next-best-action recommendation (e.g. the highest-scoring action together with the selected channel and send time).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/orchestrator.py calls propensity_agent, channel_agent, timing_agent, chooses best_action and composes the recommendation (lines 11-31).

requirement_results.requirement: The orchestrator writes the combined NBA recommendation for the customer to Azure DocumentDB.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/orchestrator.py inserts the recommendation into db.nba_recommendations using insert_one and returns the inserted id (lines 33-36).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.py reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment (lines 11-15); app/.env.example contains placeholders for DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY (lines 2-3). No actual secrets are committed.

requirement_results.requirement: .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIMS and LLM_MODEL (lines 2-5).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example sets EMBEDDING_DIMS=1536 (line 5) and seed.py stores embeddings as [0.0]*1536 (line 45); the intended vector-index dimensions equal the embedding dims. However, programmatic vector index creation failed during verification (builder_report / decisions D021) so the index itself was not created.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either (a) fix the MCP tool invocation (diagnose MCP server failure) so the sample creates the cosmosSearch vector index with dimensions matching EMBEDDING_DIMS, or (b) add a clear script/README snippet showing the exact createIndex command to run manually (include EMBEDDING_DIMS placeholder).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: README mentions non-vector indexes and notes vector index creation may be separate, but it does not provide index-parameter tuning guidance or concrete tuning instructions for larger data sets. app/seed.py does not create cosmosSearch/vector index params.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a README section describing a recommended vector index definition (kind, dimensions, similarity, maxDegree, lBuild, lSearch guidance) and show how to change those parameters when scaling (with example commands).

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.py implements a module-level _client singleton and get_client() that reuses it (lines 5-16).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/seed.py creates indexes idempotently (create_index calls lines 14-17) and uses update_one(..., upsert=True) for preferences and interactions (lines 31 and 48) so the seed can be re-run without duplication.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: The repository does not implement a /search endpoint; main.py exposes only /nba (lines 8-13).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If you add a /search endpoint, validate and return explicit 400 for empty queries and catch embedding exceptions to return informative 5xx/4xx errors; include unit tests that exercise both error cases.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No /search endpoint or vector-search code path is present; orchestration result includes only the selected action's score (orchestrator.component_scores.propensity) but not vector similarity results.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: When adding a search API, return similarity/score fields in result objects and add tests asserting the score is present and numeric.

requirement_results.evidence: app/requirements.txt lists dependencies with lower bounds (e.g. pymongo>=4.5.0) rather than exact pinned versions (app/requirements.txt lines 1-9).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Pin dependencies to exact tested versions (e.g., pymongo==4.5.0, python-dotenv==1.0.0, fastapi==0.95.0, etc.) and record them in requirements.txt / constraints.txt.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: app/tests/test_orchestrator.py contains a lightweight test that validates the orchestrate callable (lines 6-8); the test imports modules but does not require a running DocumentDB cluster.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: The repository contains no Bicep/ARM/Terraform files or IaC for Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters; the run used an existing cluster per README and decisions (D012).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add an IaC artifact (Bicep or Terraform) that provisions Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with tunable parameters (tier, storage, region) and documents low-cost defaults for local testing.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md documents what the sample shows, prerequisites and run steps (lines 1-48) but does not include explicit cleanup steps or teardown commands.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a 'Clean-up' section that shows how to remove created collections or drop the sample database (e.g. mongo shell commands or a provided cleanup.py script).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md and repository files refer to 'Azure DocumentDB' (README line 1) and do not use 'Cosmos DB' or 'Amazon DocumentDB' in code/comments.

checks.practice: Create and reuse a single, long-lived MongoClient per process (module/global singleton) instead of creating a client per request.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py implements module-level _client and get_client() singleton (lines 5-16).

checks.practice: Always require TLS for connections and validate server certificates; do not disable certificate validation in production.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example includes tls=true in the example DOCUMENTDB_URI (line 2); README instructs to set DOCUMENTDB_URI and never store secrets (README lines 16-18, 27-29).

checks.practice: Set retryWrites=false in the Azure DocumentDB connection string and verify driver-level support and implications for write retries before enabling driver-managed retryable writes.
checks.evidence: The sample relies on DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment; app/.env.example shows a tls=true URI but does not include retryWrites query parameter (app/.env.example line 2). Whether retryWrites is set in the runtime connection string cannot be determined from the repo alone.

checks.practice: Tune connection-pool parameters according to hosting context (small pools and init outside handler for serverless; larger pools and pre-warmed minPoolSize for long-running OLTP servers).
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py constructs MongoClient(uri) without explicit pool tuning options (line 15).
checks.fix: Set pool options in MongoClient from env vars (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) and document recommended defaults for serverless vs long-running processes.

checks.practice: Create indexes on fields used in filters and sorts (customer_id, action_type, channel, timestamp) and prefer well-ordered compound indexes that match common query prefixes.
checks.evidence: app/seed.py creates interactions.create_index([('customer_id',1)]) and interactions.create_index([('customer_id',1),('timestamp',-1)]) and preferences unique index on customer_id (lines 14-17).

checks.practice: Use explain('executionStats') / query plans to validate that queries are using indexes and to diagnose COLLSCAN or in-memory sorts.
checks.evidence: No code calls explain() or records query plans in the sample; this cannot be judged from repo alone.
checks.fix: Add a diagnostic script or README instruction that demonstrates running explain('executionStats') on core queries and interpreting results.

checks.practice: For vector search, create a cosmosSearch vector index (vector-diskann / vector-hnsw / vector-ivf) with dimensions and similarity that exactly match stored embeddings, and tune index parameters (maxDegree, lBuild and query-time lSearch) for the recall/latency tradeoff.
checks.evidence: seed.py stores placeholder embeddings of length 1536 (line 45) and .env.example sets EMBEDDING_DIMS=1536, but documentdb_create_index (MCP) failed and the vector cosmosSearch index was NOT created programmatically (builder_report open_issues, decision D021).
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB (public)
checks.fix: Provide a robust fallback: include an explicit createIndex command in the repo/README (with cosmosSearchOptions and placeholders), or implement a retry/diagnostic path that uses mongosh or portal instructions when MCP fails.

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB (vector-search)

checks.practice: Normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity and store embedding metadata (model name, dimensions) alongside vectors so index/query parameters remain consistent.
checks.evidence: seed.py stores an embedding field and uses EMBEDDING_DIMS=1536 in .env.example (seed.py line 45, .env.example line 5). The repo documents EMBEDDING_MODEL and EMBEDDING_DIMS in .env.example.

checks.practice: Split very large vectors or low-compressibility binary fields into a side collection keyed by document id rather than embedding them in frequently-updated core documents.
checks.evidence: This sample stores small placeholder embeddings in interactions and does not perform frequent updates that would make embedding size a problem (seed.py line 45).

checks.practice: Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds) for ephemeral documents to let the service automatically remove old demo or temporary records.
checks.evidence: The sample does not create ephemeral demo documents requiring automatic expiry; no TTL index present in seed.py.

checks.practice: Use upsert operations for idempotent writes (upsert:true) when writing recommendations to avoid duplicates and include created_at/updated_at and provenance metadata.
checks.evidence: seed.py uses update_one(..., upsert=True) for preferences and interactions (lines 31 and 48). orchestrator inserts nba_recommendations with created_at and component_scores metadata (orchestrator lines 19-31 and insert lines 33-36).

checks.practice: Project only required fields in queries (use projection) when evaluating models or agents to reduce bandwidth and latency.
checks.evidence: propensity_agent uses count_documents with full documents implied and does not use projection or projection-based aggregation; other lookups use find_one without explicit projection (agents.py lines 21-23, 38-39).
checks.fix: Use projection to fetch only the fields needed for scoring (e.g., only action_type, outcome, timestamp or use aggregation pipeline to compute counts server-side) to reduce bandwidth and improve performance.

checks.practice: Page result sets using limit and a stable sort key (e.g., timestamp desc + _id) or keyset pagination rather than relying on skip for large offsets to avoid scanning skipped documents.
checks.evidence: The sample's access patterns retrieve small per-customer aggregates and do not implement large-offset pagination.

sources.title: General Azure/MongoDB pagination guidance (avoid skip; use keyset/pagination)

checks.practice: Implement retries for transient errors with exponential backoff and jitter, honor Retry-After on 429 responses, and limit retries; combine driver retry facilities with application-level bounded retries only when operations are idempotent or deduplicated.
checks.evidence: The sample's DB calls (seed.py, orchestrator.py, agents.py) do not implement application-level retries or backoff; MongoClient default driver retries are not augmented (files: seed.py, agents.py, orchestrator.py).
checks.source: Reliability and Throttling guidance for Azure (public)
checks.fix: Add a small retry utility (exponential backoff + jitter, honoring Retry-After) and wrap transient DB calls; document when to use idempotent upserts vs non-idempotent writes.

sources.title: Reliability and Throttling guidance for Azure

checks.practice: For local development, use the DocumentDB Gateway container and configure TLS relaxation only for local dev (tlsAllowInvalidCertificates) driven by env vars; never default to disabling cert validation in code.
checks.evidence: README and .env.example instruct use of DOCUMENTDB_URI and do not relax TLS by default; README (lines 15-18) and .env.example show TLS examples (line 2).

checks.practice: Use idempotent seed scripts for demo/test data and confine test writes to the sample database (e.g., sample_customer_360_03) with the ability to run seeds repeatedly without duplication.
checks.evidence: seed.py upserts preferences and interactions using update_one(..., upsert=True) and targets sample_customer_360_03 via get_db default (seed.py lines 10-13, 31, 48).

decision_reviews.comment: Approval with operator reason '--yes' is administrative and supported by run metadata.
Choosing Python 3.10+ is supported by the run environment and prompt; events show Python available.
Choice of PyMongo and singleton client is consistent with the loaded documentdb-driver skill (events show load_skill documentdb-driver) and implementation (app/src/db.py).
Reading DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment matches the skill_md and is implemented in app/src/db.py (events show relevant skill loads).

Embedding model choice (text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims) was a model_default decision and no installed skill prescribes a specific provider/model; the repo documents this default but the decision is not grounded in an authoritative source.
Decision to make LLM usage optional was a model_default. It is defensible but not directly supported by a product doc; the sample implements deterministic heuristics accordingly.
Choosing MCP tooling to create provider-specific vector indexes matches documentdb-vector-search guidance; events show the skill was loaded and the decision is supported.
Readiness approval recorded; administrative decision.
Redundant with D002; the environment supports Python and the repo is Python-based.
PyMongo selection aligns with requirements.txt and the skill guidance; events show the driver skill was loaded.
Reading secrets from env vars is implemented and consistent with README/.env.example and skill guidance.
Decision not to provision resources is supported by the run policy and readiness notes; the build used an existing cluster (evidence in builder_report).
The simple data model (interactions, preferences, nba_recommendations) is implemented and documented (seed.py and README).

Choice of a default embedding model is model_default (see D005); no authoritative sample-default documented in installed skills. The repo documents the chosen default in .env.example but the decision is not traceable to an external source.
Decision to make agents deterministic without LLM is model_default; it is consistent with implementation (agents.py) but not mandated by a skill.
Creating standard non-vector indexes via seed.py and using MCP for vector indexes follows the skills; seed.py does create the non-vector indexes and events show vector index attempts later.
Installing dependencies via pip from requirements.txt is implemented and executed during verification (builder_report).
Running seed.py was executed and recorded in verification notes; seed script is present and idempotent.
Demo run via python main.py --demo was executed as part of verification and wrote NBA documents (builder_report).

Decision to create a cosmosSearch vector-diskann index with explicit parameters is consistent with documentdb-vector-search skill, and the repo documents the intended parameters; the actual creation failed due to a tool error (see D021).
Events show the MCP tool call failed with 'Error: Function failed.' and the builder recorded that outcome, stopped retrying and documented manual steps in the README/builder_report.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No authoritative recommendation in installed skills or repo about which embedding model to choose as a default for samples and the corresponding dimensions; builders used a model_default (text-embedding-3-small / 1536) but that choice was not grounded in a skill.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Installed skills (documentdb-vector-search, documentdb-azure-deployment), README, .env.example, Microsoft Learn searched during discovery.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample chose a default embedding model by convention. The vector index dimensions and seed embeddings were set to 1536 to match that choice, but this is a model-default choice rather than an authored team recommendation.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'Embeddings and vectors' page to the sample-guide describing recommended embedding providers/models for samples (e.g., OpenAI text-embedding-3-small 1536), the reasons for the choice (cost/quality/compatibility), and the required EMBEDDING_DIMS. Include a short table of alternatives and the dimensions required, and update .env.example with a comment linking to this page.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A tested, in-repo script that reliably creates a cosmosSearch vector index (cosmosSearchOptions) and falls back to clear manual instructions if the MCP helper call fails.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search skill, seed.py and builder_report; MCP server logs (events) show the tool failed.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The MCP call to create the vector-diskann index failed during verification and the vector index was not created; vector queries will not function until the index is created manually. This impacts any semantic/vector-enabled runs.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a seed_and_indexes.py script that attempts createIndex(...) with cosmosSearchOptions and, on failure, prints the exact mongosh command and a link to portal/CLI instructions. Include example parameters (dimensions from EMBEDDING_DIMS, similarity, maxDegree, lBuild) and a verification step (query explain or documentdb MCP verification call).

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The README lacks concrete guidance on how to change vector-index parameters for larger datasets, and does not document the trade-offs (recall vs latency) or where to adjust EMBEDDING_DIMS and maxDegree/lBuild.
doc_gaps.where_searched: app/README.md, documentdb-vector-search skill materials, and discovery notes.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Users will not know how to reconfigure the vector index for larger data sizes and may attempt to create incompatible indexes. The sample's index-creation fallback is documented only in the open_issues/builder_report text, not in the README.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Extend README with a 'Vector index tuning' subsection showing example parameters for small, medium, and large datasets, recommended lBuild/lSearch values, and pointers to the documentdb-vector-search skill and portal UI for index creation and monitoring.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The sample did not include an application-level retry wrapper (exponential backoff + jitter) or guidance to honor Retry-After for 429s.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb reliability docs, documentdb-monitoring skill, repository code.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Transient errors and throttling are not handled at the application level; in real runs this could cause failures or poor reliability under load.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Ship an agent-kit rule and a small library (retry_util.py) demonstrating exponential backoff + jitter, honoring Retry-After, and using idempotent upserts for retriable operations. Include one-line guidance in README pointing to the retry helper.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The repo's requirements.txt uses >= bounds rather than exact pins. There is no constraints file or note showing which tested versions the sample was validated against.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Reproducibility risk: different installs may pull incompatible versions leading to test or runtime failures.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide a pinned requirements.txt (exact versions) and an optional constraints.txt. Add a README note that records the working versions used during verification and a command to freeze them (pip freeze > requirements.txt) for CI.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The seed script performs per-document upserts in a loop rather than batching writes (bulk_write) for larger seeds.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: For the small demo data set this is acceptable, but for larger sample data it would be inefficient and slow.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide an alternative seed_bulk.py that uses insert_many/bulk_write in size-limited batches and documents when to use upserts vs insert_many.

doc_gaps.topic: Unit test mocking strategy for LLM/cluster
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No documented mocking strategy for LLM/embedding calls or for MongoDB MCP when running unit tests offline; the sample's single test is synthetic and does not demonstrate how to mock the DB or LLM.
doc_gaps.where_searched: app/tests, README, and installed skills; no sample test guidelines found.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Tests passed in this run because they are minimal, but maintainers will need guidance to write robust offline tests that exercise agents when LLM/cluster are not available.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add testing examples using mongomock for DB interactions and monkeypatching/mocking for LangChain/embedding calls. Include an example pytest fixture that sets up mongomock.DB and environment variables for offline runs.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Explicit cleanup instructions (how to drop collections or the sample database) are not present in README.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Users may leave demo artifacts in their cluster; cleanup steps make it safe to re-run samples and free resources.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'Clean-up' section showing mongosh/mongo client commands to drop nba_recommendations, interactions and preferences or a provided cleanup.py script to drop the sample database.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: An example IaC template (Bicep/Terraform) targeting Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters was not included in the repo.
doc_gaps.where_searched: repository root and documentdb-azure-deployment skill docs.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builders who want to provision reproducible test clusters must author IaC themselves; using incorrect resource types risks provisioning the wrong service (Cosmos DB vs DocumentDB).
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Ship a small Bicep example (mongoCluster.bicep) showing Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameters (tier, storage, region) and defaults for low-cost dev; include a README pointer explaining the difference between mongoClusters and older databaseAccounts examples.
